rulings.model: Form 8915-F must also be filed when 'A qualified disaster distribution was made to you from an eligible retirement plan' in 'this year' (2025). It also covers qualified distributions for a main home. The question covers only distributions taken in 2023 or 2024.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: interface gap; a qualified disaster distribution made in 2025, and a 2025 qualified distribution for a main home, come on a 2025 Form 1099-R and are screened per form by retirement.disaster ("Did you take this money out, or put money back, because of a federally declared disaster (Form 8915-F)?"), refused through retirement.special ("Forms 5329, 8606, 4972, 8915-F"). scope.disaster_distribution covers the earlier-year cases of i8915f p. 2, Who Must File, "A qualified disaster distribution was made to you in a prior year that you are including in income in equal amounts over 3 years and 'this year' is a year within the 3-year period"; a 2022 distribution's three years end in 2024. Checked residual: a late-2025 repayment of a 2022 distribution goes on the 2025 Form 8915-F but, with no 2025 income from it, is carried back (i8915f p. 8, Carrybacks), leaving the 2025 tax unchanged. The reviewer saw only scope. Project stands.

Form 8582 says passive activities include 'Trade or business activities in which you did not materially participate for the tax year,' with no prior-year ownership condition, so a business first owned in 2025 without material participation (for example on Schedule C) would never be screened.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; the reviewer is right that f8582's passive activities carry no prior-year ownership condition, but each activity begun in 2025 is screened where it is entered: a Schedule C business in which the filer did not materially participate is refused by sc.screened (sc.passive false; i1040sc p. 4, Line G, the seven tests), a farm or a K-1 by scope.schedule1 (scope.farm, scope.k1), and a rental of real property is now computed with its passive loss limit (Schedule E with Form 8582, this merge: f8582, rental.active). The gated question catches what those do not: a passive activity owned before 2025 with prior-year unallowed losses or a 2025 disposition, the case its wording (no longer 'or rental') names. As in the landing render ruling, now with rentals computed rather than refused. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the reviewer's points are checked against p525 p. 24, Recoveries: "A recovery is a return of an amount you deducted or took a credit for in an earlier year" and Tax benefit rule, "up to the amount by which the deduction or credit you took for the recovered amount reduced your tax in the earlier year". The "lowered your tax" condition is the source's, but the question names only a deduction, so a recovery of an amount taken as a credit is answered No and left off Schedule 1 line 8z; and it excepts only "a state income tax refund", while Schedule 1 line 1 and the refund form (refund.any, "state or local income tax") cover local income tax refunds, so a filer with a city or county income tax refund is refused needlessly.
